scoring.summary: Score 0-100 = weighted blend of five sub-scores, each scaled 0-1. Analyst data says where the price could go; technicals say whether now is a sensible entry.
filters: At least 5 analysts covering the stock
At least 220 trading days of price history

components.name: Analyst upside
components.rule: Upside = average analyst target / price - 1. 0% or less scores 0; 50% or more scores 1; linear in between.

components.name: Analyst consensus
components.rule: Mean rating on a 1 (sell) to 5 (strong buy) scale, rescaled to 0-1, then multiplied by min(1, analysts/10) so thinly covered stocks are discounted.

components.name: Trend
components.rule: 0.5 if price > 200-day MA, plus 0.5 if 50-day MA > 200-day MA.

components.name: RSI(14) setup
components.rule: Peaks at RSI 45 (a pullback that isn't a free-fall): score = 1 - |RSI - 45| / 35, floored at 0. So RSI 10 or RSI 80 scores 0.

components.name: Volume accumulation
components.rule: Share of the last 20 days' volume traded on up-days. 30% or less scores 0, 70% or more scores 1.

scoring.caveat: A screen, not advice. It ranks large caps by a transparent rule; it does not know about news, earnings dates or your risk tolerance.
